FITASC: how the international federation was born

FITASC is short for the French name Fédération Internationale de Tir aux Armes Sportives de Chasse. In English that is roughly the International Federation for Shooting with Sporting Hunting Guns. The name shows its roots in hunting.

The federation was founded on 4 June 1921 in Lausanne, Switzerland. Its first name was the International Union of Hunting (UIC). National groups from ten countries in Europe, Africa and America took part in the first meeting. They wanted one set of rules, so that shooters from different countries could compete against each other on equal terms.

The General Assembly (the meeting of all its member organisations) renamed the union FITASC in 1938, and the name has stayed. Its headquarters are in Paris. That is why some sources say FITASC was founded in Paris: Paris is its home, but the founding meeting was held in Lausanne.

FITASC brings together the national federations of many countries. A shooter is usually not a direct member: you join a club and a national federation, and the federation is a member of FITASC.

FITASC's main job is the rules. It writes and updates the international rules of Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting. It does the same for other disciplines, such as Universal Trench (a trap-style discipline with five machines in a trench) and Helice (shot at spinning plastic targets with wings). Many national federations base their own events on these rules.

FITASC also keeps the international calendar and decides where and when the World and European Championships are held. It approves the layouts of international Sporting™ competitions. And it keeps an eye on the referees: the chief referee of an international event needs a FITASC qualification.

Do not confuse FITASC with the ISSF, the International Shooting Sport Federation. The ISSF governs the Olympic disciplines, including Olympic Trap and Skeet. FITASC's own history page says that since 1969 both Olympic clay disciplines have been run by the ISSF (which was then called the UIT).

Tip: How the sport is organised today, from the club to world level: FITASC and how international shooting is organised.

Key points

  • FITASC was founded on 4 June 1921 in Lausanne, Switzerland; its headquarters are in Paris.
  • Its members are national federations, not individual shooters.
  • FITASC writes the rules of Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting and keeps the international calendar.
  • Olympic Trap and Skeet are governed by the ISSF, not by FITASC.

Did you know?

FITASC got its present name in 1938. For its first 17 years it was the International Union of Hunting.

Check yourself · 3 questions

  1. Where was the founding meeting of FITASC held in 1921?

    1. In Paris, France
    2. In Lausanne, Switzerland
    3. In London, England
    Answer

    In Lausanne, Switzerland

    The founding meeting was in Lausanne on 4 June 1921; Paris is FITASC's home today.

  2. Who are the members of FITASC?

    1. Individual shooters
    2. Gun makers
    3. National federations
    Answer

    National federations

    FITASC unites national federations; a shooter belongs to a club and to their own federation.

  3. Which federation governs Olympic Trap and Skeet?

    1. The ISSF
    2. FITASC
    3. Each national club
    Answer

    The ISSF

    The ISSF governs the Olympic disciplines; FITASC governs Sporting™, Compak® Sporting and other non-Olympic ones.
